key.system:
You are the intake clerk at a law firm. You read one intake document, a document that has just arrived and has not yet been classified, and decide its document type so it can be sent to the right team.

The document may come with a cover note or email from the client. Classify the document itself, not the note; use the note only as context.

Decide the document type by the document's PRIMARY PURPOSE: what the document as a whole is mainly for. Do not decide by its title alone, by a single clause, or by which topics it mentions.

Document types:

nda
  A non-disclosure or confidentiality agreement: its main purpose is to protect confidential information that one or both parties disclose, usually so they can evaluate or discuss a possible deal. Most of its clauses define confidential information and the obligations to keep it secret.

msa
  A master services agreement: the framework terms under which one party provides services to another over time (services standard, fees and payment, intellectual property, liability, term and termination), usually with specific work ordered later under statements of work.

dpa
  A data processing agreement: its main purpose is to govern how one party processes personal data on behalf of another (instructions, security, sub-processors, breach notification, data subject rights, international transfers), as data protection law requires.

sow
  A statement of work: it orders one specific project or engagement under an existing master agreement, setting out its scope, deliverables, milestones, acceptance and fees for that project.

other
  Anything whose primary purpose is none of the above: for example a letter of intent, term sheet, lease, employment contract, settlement, or general correspondence.

A hybrid document still has exactly one document type. Many documents touch several topics: an MSA often has a confidentiality section, a SOW may mention personal data, a letter of intent may include a binding confidentiality paragraph. Those sections do not change the type. Ask what the document is mainly for, and choose that one type.

Worked example: a master services agreement setting the terms on which a supplier provides software services, which also contains a confidentiality section, has primary purpose "framework for services". Its document type is "msa", not "nda".

Give a short rationale (one or two sentences) naming the primary purpose that decided the type.
key.prompt:
Classify the document type of this intake document.

<intake-document id="intake-gen-10">
# Master Services and Consulting Agreement

## 1. Parties and Background

[1.1] This agreement is entered into by Mossgate Pharmacy Holdings plc ("Mossgate" or the "Customer") and Tarnwick Technology Services Ltd ("Tarnwick" or the "Supplier").

[1.2] Mossgate wishes to appoint Tarnwick as a non-exclusive provider of professional services over the term of this agreement. No services are ordered by this agreement itself: the Customer orders specific work by signing a statement of work, which states its scope, deliverables, timetable and fees, and these master terms govern every statement of work.

## 2. Statements of Work

[2.1] The Customer may request services at any time by sending the Supplier a draft statement of work. The Supplier shall respond within ten working days, either accepting the draft or proposing changes to it, and no statement of work takes effect until signed by an authorised representative of each party.

[2.2] Where a statement of work and these master terms are inconsistent, these master terms take precedence.

## 3. Services

[3.1] The Supplier shall provide the services in accordance with each statement of work and any service levels it sets out, and shall comply with the Customer's reasonable site rules when working at the Customer's premises.

[3.2] If the Supplier expects to miss a date set out in a statement of work, it shall notify the Customer promptly, explain the cause, and propose a plan to recover the delay.

## 4. Personnel

[4.1] The Supplier shall name a delivery manager for each statement of work, who shall be the Customer's day-to-day contact. The Supplier shall not replace the delivery manager, or any other key person named in a statement of work, without the Customer's prior consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

## 5. Fees and Payment

[5.1] The Customer shall pay the fees set out in each statement of work. Unless a statement of work states otherwise, the Supplier shall invoice monthly in arrears and the Customer shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty days of receipt.

[5.2] The Customer shall notify any disputed amount within fifteen days of receiving the invoice, giving its reasons, and the parties shall try in good faith to resolve the dispute promptly.

## 6. Intellectual Property

[6.1] The Supplier owns its tools, methods and know-how, including any it improves while performing the services. On payment, the Customer owns the deliverables named in each statement of work, and receives a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence of any Supplier material incorporated in them, for its own business purposes.

## 7. Liability

[7.1] Neither party limits its liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud. Subject to that, each party's total liability in each twelve-month period from the date this agreement starts is limited to the fees paid or payable in that period under all statements of work, and neither party is liable for indirect or consequential loss.

## 8. Term and Termination

[8.1] This agreement starts on signature and continues until terminated. Either party may end it on ninety days' written notice, but a statement of work in force at that time continues on these terms until its services are complete.

[8.2] The Customer may end a statement of work early on thirty days' notice, and shall then pay for the services performed up to the date of termination.

## 9. General

[9.1] This agreement, together with each statement of work, is the entire agreement between the parties about its subject matter. Any variation must be in writing and signed by both parties. This agreement is governed by the laws of England and Wales.
</intake-document>

value.rationale: The document's primary purpose is to set framework terms (services standards, personnel, fees, IP, liability, term and termination) under which the supplier provides professional services over time, with specific work to be ordered later through statements of work. It is a master services agreement, not an NDA, SOW, or DPA, despite having no dedicated confidentiality or data protection sections.
